# 100proof

> 100proof (entered in the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 as 100 Proof) is a home inventory app for insurance. A person films each room on a phone, and Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 turns the video into a room-by-room inventory with counts, brands, models, replacement cost in the property's zip, and actual cash value. When the video cannot confirm a line, 100proof asks for the one thing that would: a label photo, a wider shot, a receipt, or an answer.

The public site is https://100proof.tech. The guide for homeowners, renters, insurers, and administrators, with sources, is https://100proof.tech/information.

## For homeowners and renters

- Five minutes on a phone: film each room, with no typing and nothing to install.
- Each line gets brand, model, count, replacement cost new in the property's zip, and actual cash value after wear.
- It says what it could not see and asks for what would confirm it, instead of guessing.
- The video stays with the account, every line shows where it came from, and the record is sealed with a fingerprint when it is created.
- Download a CSV or a JSON claim file, email it, or send it. Film again at renewal.
- Private by default: clips and pictures in private storage; exact device location never saved; personal data not sold.

## For insurers, adjusters, claims administrators, agents, and property managers

- Files arrive reviewable: each line keeps its sources apart (camera, what the policyholder said, receipt, comparable) with a change history.
- Anything that could not be confirmed is flagged at the top of the file.
- Valuation follows the adjuster method: replacement cost for like kind and quality at local prices, and actual cash value after physical depreciation. The exact product, or a labeled comparable.
- Contents documented at bind and renewal, before a loss.
- Output as CSV and a versioned JSON claim file. Request a connection from the For providers tab on the home page.

## Models

Muse Spark 1.3 reviews the video, prices each line, and reads labels, receipts, and answers. Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0 captures what the person says while filming. Every model answer is checked before it reaches the inventory.

## Accuracy

100proof does not claim 100% accuracy. Every line shows whether its count and its model are confirmed, and lines that cannot be confirmed are flagged for review rather than guessed.

## What 100proof is not

- Not an insurance company, an adjuster, or a public adjuster. It does not interpret a policy, negotiate with an insurer, or decide coverage or payment. The insurer decides.
- Not a program of the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, the Texas Department of Insurance, or any government. Those offices tell people to make a home inventory; 100proof is one way to do it.
- Not certified by Meta. It uses named Meta models.

## Facts with sources, checked 2026-10-29

- NAIC consumer guide: inventory every room with photos or video, store it away from the home, and update it every year. https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/publication-hoi-pp-consumer-homeowners.pdf
- Triple-I / Munich Re 2023 survey: 47% of homeowners said they had prepared an inventory of their possessions. https://www.iii.org/fact-statistic/facts-statistics-homeowners-and-renters-insurance
- Texas Department of Insurance: a missing inventory can delay a contents claim; a phone video of each room is a valid start. https://www.tdi.texas.gov/tips/home-inventory.html
- J.D. Power 2026 U.S. Property Claims Satisfaction Study: 40.7 days on average from first notice of loss to final payment. https://www.jdpower.com/business/press-releases/2026-us-property-claims-satisfaction-study/
- California Department of Insurance, 2025 Los Angeles wildfires: insurers were asked to advance at least 75% of contents limits without an inventory. The remainder still needed a list. https://www.insurance.ca.gov/0400-news/0100-press-releases/2025/release014-2025.cfm
- US contents coverage paid for and not collected because it was not documented: $3–7 billion a year. This is 100proof's own conservative estimate, not a government statistic.
